source: Money Rooms v3 spec, Measure, plus Level 9 (What Moves the FI Date): standard FI metrics with direction, levers and graph links

metrics.name: Take-home monthly
metrics.clientLabel: What lands in the bank each month
metrics.definition: Pay after taxes and payroll deductions, per month.

levers.text: Raise pay or cut payroll deductions that do not come back.
A raise or a second income lifts take-home.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your what lands in the bank each month: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Gross monthly
metrics.definition: Pay before taxes and deductions, per month, bonus and equity included.

levers.text: A raise, a bonus or a second income.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your pay before anything comes out: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Monthly spending
metrics.definition: Every spending line per month, plus insurance premiums paid from the bank. Line items override a rough total.
metrics.formula: sum(spending lines, monthly) + sum(safety premiums not via payroll)

levers.text: Lower any spending line, the big three first: housing, transportation, food.
Shop insurance premiums paid from the bank.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your what a month costs: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Surplus
metrics.definition: Take-home minus spending minus debt minimums.

levers.text: More take-home.
Less spending.
A paid-off debt frees its minimum.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your left over each month: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Savings rate (take-home)
metrics.definition: (take-home minus spending) divided by take-home.

levers.text: Cut spending: each dollar raises the rate twice as fast as a dollar earned.
Earn more and keep the spending flat.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your share of take-home saved: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Savings rate (gross, FIRE style)
metrics.clientLabel: Share of total pay saved, match included
metrics.definition: (pre-tax contributions + match + take-home minus spending) divided by (gross + match).
metrics.formula: (pretaxContrib + roth + hsa + match + takeHome - spending) / (gross + match)

range.source: Mr. Money Mustache, The Shockingly Simple Math

levers.text: Raise the 401k deferral.
Capture the full match.
Spend less.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your share of total pay saved, match included: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Leak rate
metrics.clientLabel: Money the math says is left but does not land in savings
metrics.definition: Surplus the math says, minus savings actually landing in accounts, as a share of take-home.

levers.text: Give the surplus a landing: an automatic transfer the day after payday.
Find the lines the leak hides in.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your money the math says is left but does not land in savings: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: DRAFTT shares
metrics.definition: Debt, Retirement, Accommodation, Food, Transportation, Therapy as shares of take-home (Retirement over gross).

levers.text: Each share falls when its lines fall.
Retirement share rises with deferrals.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your where each dollar goes: {value}. This one is a shape to read, not a score to beat.

metrics.name: FAT floor
metrics.definition: Food, accommodation and transportation lines kept in a lean month.
metrics.formula: sum(spending lines flagged in FAT floor)

levers.text: Lower the flagged lines: rent, groceries, transit.
Flag only what a lean month truly needs.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your the lean month: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Shelter rate
metrics.definition: Accommodation (rent or mortgage plus utilities) divided by take-home.

range.source: The 30% rule of thumb, widened for high-cost cities

levers.text: A cheaper place, a roommate or a house hack.

sources.label: My default: housing at or under 35% of take-home (Assumptions)

metrics.gentleCopy: Your housing share of take-home: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Fixed-cost rate
metrics.clientLabel: Share of take-home already spoken for
metrics.definition: Spending lines marked need, plus bank-paid premiums, divided by take-home.

range.source: Ramit Sethi conscious-spending plan: fixed costs 50 to 60%

levers.text: Turn a fixed need into a flexible want where you can.
Mark lines honestly as needs or wants.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your share of take-home already spoken for: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Real hourly wage
metrics.clientLabel: What an hour of work really pays
metrics.definition: (take-home minus costs of working) divided by (paid plus commute and prep hours).

levers.text: Cut the costs of working: commute, clothes, convenience food.
A shorter commute raises the real wage.
More pay for the same hours.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your what an hour of work really pays: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Monthly debt service
metrics.definition: Sum of minimum payments.

levers.text: Pay a debt off and its minimum goes away.
Lower balances carry lower minimums.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your debt payments each month: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Total debt
metrics.definition: Sum of balances.

levers.text: Pay balances down, highest rate first.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your everything owed: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Debt-to-income
metrics.clientLabel: Debt payments as a share of pay
metrics.definition: Monthly debt service divided by gross monthly.

levers.text: Lower minimums.
Higher gross pay.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your debt payments as a share of pay: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Debt-to-assets
metrics.definition: Total debt divided by total assets.

levers.text: Pay debt down.
Grow assets.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your owed versus owned: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Weighted APR
metrics.definition: Balance-weighted interest rate, promo rate while a promo runs.

levers.text: Refinance or move the highest-rate balance first.
A lower loan rate.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your average interest rate, by balance: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Annual interest cost
metrics.definition: Interest on today's balances over the next 12 months, promo rate until the promo ends; a card on full autopay carries none.

levers.text: Pay the highest APR first; a promo or a transfer lowers it.
Lower balances pay less interest.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your interest over the next year: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Credit utilization
metrics.definition: Card balances over credit limits, total and per card.

range.source: CFPB and FICO guidance: under 30%, under 10% best

levers.text: Pay the card down before the statement closes.
A higher limit lowers utilization.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your how full the cards are: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Promo cliff
metrics.definition: For each promo: months left and what the balance costs a year at the standard rate.
metrics.formula: balance x standardApr; months until promoEnd

levers.text: Clear the promo balance before the cliff.
A later promo end buys time.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your when a 0% offer ends: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Debt-free date and freed cash flow
metrics.definition: Month the last debt is paid at current minimums, freed payments rolled to the next debt (avalanche), and the cash freed by month.

levers.text: Pay more than the minimum, highest rate first.
A lower rate finishes sooner.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your when the last payment lands: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Net worth
metrics.definition: Total assets minus total debt.

levers.text: Invest the surplus.
Pay debt down.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your owned minus owed: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Total, invested and liquid assets
metrics.clientLabel: What is owned, and how much of it moves
metrics.definition: Total assets; the part that takes market returns; the part reachable without penalty.

levers.text: Contributions and growth.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your what is owned, and how much of it moves: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Liquidity rate
metrics.definition: Liquid assets divided by total assets.

levers.text: Hold some savings in a taxable account or cash.
Reachable account types raise the share.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your share of assets reachable now: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Bridge years
metrics.definition: Liquid plus semi-liquid assets divided by annual spending.

levers.text: Taxable and Roth balances bridge the years before 59.5.
Lower spending stretches the bridge.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your years the reachable money covers: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Runway months
metrics.definition: Cash divided by monthly spending at full spending, at needs only, and at the FAT floor.

levers.text: Build cash to the Rule of 5 target.
A lower FAT floor stretches the runway.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your how long cash lasts: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Rule of 5 target
metrics.definition: Age divided by five, in months of spending.

levers.text: Lower spending lowers the target.
The target grows with age.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your cash to keep on hand: {value}. This one is a shape to read, not a score to beat.

metrics.name: Emergency gap and monthly to close
metrics.definition: Rule of 5 target minus cash, floored at zero, and a twelfth of it.

levers.text: Send the surplus to cash until the gap closes.
Lower spending lowers the target.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your cash still to set aside: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Excess cash drag
metrics.clientLabel: What idle cash costs a year
metrics.definition: Cash above the Rule of 5 target times the gap between the likely real return and the cash real return.

levers.text: Move cash above the target into investments.
The gap between returns sets the drag.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your what idle cash costs a year: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Tax-advantaged share
metrics.definition: Pre-tax, Roth and HSA balances divided by total assets.

levers.text: Fill pre-tax room first.
Roth and HSA contributions.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your assets inside tax shelters: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Tax bucket mix
metrics.definition: Balances by tax bucket as shares of total assets.

levers.text: Direct new money to the bucket that is thin.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your pre-tax, Roth, taxable, cash: {value}. This one is a shape to read, not a score to beat.

metrics.name: Match capture and match left
metrics.definition: Match received divided by match available, and the dollars left a year.

levers.text: Defer at least up to the match.
The plan sets how much is matched.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your free money taken, and left: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Room left under limits
metrics.clientLabel: Space left in each account this year
metrics.definition: Each limit minus this year's contributions.

levers.text: Raise the deferral.
IRA and HSA contributions use the room.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your space left in each account this year: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Weighted expense ratio
metrics.definition: Dollar-weighted expense ratio across holdings.

levers.text: Swap to a lower-cost fund in the same account.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your average fund fee: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Fee drag, lifetime
metrics.clientLabel: What fund fees cost by retirement
metrics.definition: Today's invested balance grown to retirement age at the likely return, minus the same at the return less fees.

levers.text: A lower expense ratio compounds for decades.
More invested means more fee.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your what fund fees cost by retirement: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Allocation
metrics.definition: Dollar-weighted stocks, bonds, cash and other across accounts, and the US share of stocks.

levers.text: Rebalance toward the target mix.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your stocks, bonds, cash: {value}. This one is a shape to read, not a score to beat.

metrics.name: Implied tax rate
metrics.clientLabel: Share of pay that goes to taxes
metrics.definition: (gross minus take-home minus payroll deductions) divided by gross, from the paystub.

levers.text: Pre-tax deferrals lower the implied rate.
Check the paystub for over-withholding.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your share of pay that goes to taxes: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Effective and marginal federal rate
metrics.clientLabel: Federal tax, average and on the next dollar
metrics.definition: Estimated federal tax divided by gross, and the bracket of the last dollar.

levers.text: Pre-tax deferrals lower taxable income.
HSA contributions are pre-tax.
Filing status sets the brackets.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your federal tax, average and on the next dollar: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: FICA
metrics.definition: Social Security and Medicare on wages; both halves for self-employment.
metrics.formula: wages x 7.65% up to the wage base, plus Medicare above

levers.text: HSA and section 125 lines skip FICA.
FICA follows wages.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your social Security and Medicare tax: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Tax saved per $1,000 pre-tax
metrics.definition: The marginal rate times 1,000 (plus FICA where the deduction avoids it).

levers.text: A higher bracket saves more per pre-tax dollar.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your what each $1,000 into a 401k saves: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: FI number
metrics.clientLabel: The portfolio that pays for life
metrics.definition: Annual spending divided by the withdrawal rate.

levers.text: Every $100 a month cut lowers the number by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100.
A higher withdrawal rate lowers the number and raises the risk.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your the portfolio that pays for life: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: % to FI
metrics.definition: Net worth (or invested assets, by the FI progress basis assumption) divided by the FI number, on the same line as the FI date.

levers.text: Invest more.
Lower spending lowers the target.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your how far along: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Coast FI number and %
metrics.definition: The FI number discounted to today at the likely return over the years to retirement age, and the FI progress basis against it.

levers.text: A later retirement age lowers the coast number.
A higher return assumption lowers it.
Lower spending lowers it.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your enough today to coast: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: FI date and years to FI
metrics.clientLabel: When the portfolio could carry the household
metrics.definition: First projection year where net worth times the withdrawal rate covers spending, at the likely, best and worst returns. Goals spend their cost in the year they land, so a goal moved or resized moves this date.
metrics.formula: projection, year by year to 95, with the goals spent along the way

levers.text: Spending cuts move the date twice: a smaller target and more saved.
Invest more each month.
Earn more and invest the difference.
Returns are not a lever, only an assumption.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your when the portfolio could carry the household: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Lean, Fat and Barista FI
metrics.definition: Alias of the FI ladder (MR-040): Lean, FI, Fat and Barista as one list for the gauge and older records.
metrics.formula: fatFloor x 12 / wr; spending x 12 x fat / wr; (spending x 12 - barista) / wr

levers.text: Lower spending lowers every rung.
Part-time income lowers the Barista rungs.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your three sizes of enough: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Value of one more point
metrics.clientLabel: What one more percent saved buys
metrics.definition: Months the FI date moves earlier when the savings rate rises by one point of take-home.

levers.text: One more point of take-home saved.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your what one more percent saved buys: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Card net value
metrics.clientLabel: Is each card worth its fee
metrics.definition: Credits actually used plus rewards on actual spending minus the annual fee, per card.

levers.text: A card that fits the spending.
Use the credits you pay for.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your is each card worth its fee: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Rewards left on the table
metrics.clientLabel: Rewards the spending could earn elsewhere
metrics.definition: For each spending line with a card, the best library earn rate for its category minus the actual, a year.
metrics.formula: sum((best rate - actual rate) x spend x 12)

levers.text: Pay each category with the card that earns most there.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your rewards the spending could earn elsewhere: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Lean FI number
metrics.definition: The FAT floor (food, accommodation, transportation) a year over the withdrawal rate. Percent there, the date the projection reaches it, and the monthly investing that reaches it by the dream FI age.

levers.text: Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.
Flag only what a lean month truly needs.
A higher withdrawal rate lowers every number and raises the risk.
Invested balances count toward every rung.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your the floor: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Barista Lean FI number
metrics.definition: Lean FI minus part-time income a year over the withdrawal rate.

levers.text: Every $100 a month of part-time income lowers the target by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100.
Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.
A higher withdrawal rate lowers every number and raises the risk.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your the floor, with part-time work: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Barista FI number
metrics.definition: The FI number minus part-time income a year over the withdrawal rate.

levers.text: Every $100 a month of part-time income lowers the target by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100.
Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.
A higher withdrawal rate lowers every number and raises the risk.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your enough, with part-time work: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: FI number (ladder rung)
metrics.definition: Spending a year on the chosen basis (actual, gut or dream) over the withdrawal rate; the same number as the FI number, with percent there, date and required monthly.

levers.text: Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.
A higher withdrawal rate lowers every number and raises the risk.
Invested balances count toward every rung.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your enough: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Fat FI number
metrics.definition: Dream spending a year over the withdrawal rate; spending times the fat multiplier when no dream is typed.

levers.text: A more modest dream is a closer rung.
A higher withdrawal rate lowers every number and raises the risk.
Invested balances count toward every rung.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your the dream: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Barista rule of thumb
metrics.definition: Every $100 a month of part-time income lowers the FI target by 100 x 12 over the withdrawal rate: $30,000 at 4%, $34,286 at 3.5%.

levers.text: A higher withdrawal rate lowers every number and raises the risk.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your what part-time work is worth: {value}. This one is a shape to read, not a score to beat.

metrics.name: Part-time income to be Barista FI today
metrics.clientLabel: Part-time pay that would make today enough
metrics.definition: Spending a month minus what invested assets pay at the withdrawal rate; the same for the Lean floor.

levers.text: Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.
Invested balances count toward every rung.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your part-time pay that would make today enough: {value}. This one is a shape to read, not a score to beat.

metrics.name: FI ratio
metrics.clientLabel: Share of spending the portfolio already covers
metrics.definition: Investment income at the withdrawal rate plus rental income over annual spending. 1.0 is FI.

levers.text: Invested balances count toward every rung.
Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.
Rental income counts toward the ratio.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your share of spending the portfolio already covers: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Crossover date
metrics.clientLabel: When the money starts paying for life
metrics.definition: The first month net worth at the withdrawal rate covers spending, on the projection: the FI date, to the month.
metrics.formula: first month netWorth x withdrawalRate >= spending x 12

levers.text: Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.
More invested each month pulls the crossover closer.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your when the money starts paying for life: {value}. This one is a shape to read, not a score to beat.

metrics.name: Days of freedom
metrics.clientLabel: Days the portfolio could pay for
metrics.definition: Invested assets divided by one day of spending.

levers.text: Invested balances count toward every rung.
Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your days the portfolio could pay for: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Years of expenses
metrics.clientLabel: Years the portfolio could pay for
metrics.definition: Invested assets divided by annual spending. 25 is FI at 4%.

levers.text: Invested balances count toward every rung.
Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your years the portfolio could pay for: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: The flip (invested only)
metrics.clientLabel: When growth beats what you add (invested only)
metrics.definition: The first projection year the portfolio grows more from returns than from contributions. Counts invested assets only, not cash or debt, so it can sit far from the FI date.
metrics.formula: first year invested x return > contributions

levers.text: Invested balances count toward every rung.
Odd but true: more contributions push the flip later and FI closer.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your when growth beats what you add (invested only): {value}. This one is a shape to read, not a score to beat.

metrics.name: First $100,000
metrics.definition: The projected month net worth reaches $100,000, on the same line as the FI date.

levers.text: Invested balances count toward every rung.
More invested each month.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your when the first $100,000 lands: {value}. This one is a shape to read, not a score to beat.

metrics.name: True FI number (after tax)
metrics.definition: The invested amount whose withdrawals, taxed as ordinary income on the pre-tax share of the bucket mix, cover spending after tax.
metrics.formula: withdrawals W where W - federalTax(W x pretaxShare) = spending x 12; W / withdrawalRate

levers.text: Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.
Roth and taxable dollars need no tax room at withdrawal.
A higher withdrawal rate lowers every number and raises the risk.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your enough, after tax: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: FI number with Social Security
metrics.definition: The FI number with Social Security as an income floor from the claim age; the bridge years before it are funded from the portfolio.
metrics.formula: (spending - ss) x 12 / withdrawalRate + ss x 12 x bridgeYears

levers.text: Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.
The share of the scheduled benefit you count on.
Claiming later raises the benefit and lengthens the bridge.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your enough, counting Social Security: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Health care bridge to 65
metrics.definition: The pre-65 premium estimate times the years from the FI date to 65.

levers.text: A lower premium estimate, or a plan with subsidies.
Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your health insurance before Medicare: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Wealth multiplier
metrics.clientLabel: What a dollar invested today becomes
metrics.definition: (1 + real return) to the years until retirement age: what one dollar invested today is worth then.

levers.text: More years to compound.
An assumption, not a lever.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your what a dollar invested today becomes: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: A purchase in FI days
metrics.clientLabel: What a purchase costs in time
metrics.definition: A $1,000 one-time cost as days of FI date delay, and $100 a month recurring as FI number cost.
metrics.formula: 1000 / (fiNumber x return + contributions) x 365; 100 x 12 / withdrawalRate

levers.text: Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.
Invested balances count toward every rung.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your what a purchase costs in time: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Expected net worth (Millionaire Next Door)
metrics.definition: Age times annual gross income over ten, and actual net worth against it. Coach view by default.
metrics.formula: age x gross x 12 / 10; netWorth / that

levers.text: Invest the surplus.
Pay debt down.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your expected net worth: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Salary multiple vs benchmark
metrics.definition: Invested assets over annual gross pay against the age benchmark from the chosen source. Coach view by default.

levers.text: Invested balances count toward every rung.
More invested each month.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your saved, in years of pay: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Savings rate needed for the dream FI age
metrics.clientLabel: Share of take-home to save for the dream
metrics.definition: The monthly investing that reaches the FI number by the dream FI age, as a share of take-home.

levers.text: Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.
A later dream age needs a lower rate.
More take-home.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your share of take-home to save for the dream: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Monthly investing for the dream FI age
metrics.definition: The monthly investing that takes invested assets to the FI number by the dream FI age at the likely return.
metrics.formula: (fiNumber - invested x g) x r / (12 x (g - 1)), g = (1 + r) ^ years

levers.text: Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.
A later dream age needs less each month.
Invested balances count toward every rung.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your monthly investing for the dream: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Guardrails spending band
metrics.definition: The spending range in retirement that keeps the withdrawal rate within the band of its starting rate.
metrics.formula: spending x (1 - band) to spending x (1 + band)

levers.text: Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.
A wider band means more flex and more risk.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your room to spend in retirement: {value}. This one is a shape to read, not a score to beat.

metrics.name: Gut gap as FI date
metrics.definition: The gut guess of monthly spending against the lines, expressed as FI number and months of FI date.
metrics.formula: (gut - spending) x 12 / withdrawalRate; / annual growth near FI x 12

levers.text: The gut guess itself.
Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your gut guess against the lines: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Dream gap as FI date
metrics.definition: Dream spending against the lines, expressed as FI number and months of FI date.
metrics.formula: (dream - spending) x 12 / withdrawalRate; / annual growth near FI x 12

levers.text: The dream itself.
Every $100 a month cut lowers this rung by 12 / withdrawal rate x 100 and adds $100 to savings.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your dream against today: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Doubling time
metrics.definition: 72 over the real return in percent.

levers.text: An assumption, not a lever.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your years for money to double: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Big three share
metrics.clientLabel: Housing, food and getting around as a share of pay
metrics.definition: Housing, food and transportation together, divided by take-home.

range.source: The big three: under half of take-home leaves room to save

levers.text: Housing is the lever that moves this most; food and transport are the two you can move this month.
More take-home shrinks the share without touching a line.

sources.label: The big three: under half of take-home leaves room to save

metrics.gentleCopy: Your housing, food and getting around as a share of pay: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: A month of spending in hours of work
metrics.clientLabel: Hours of work a month of life costs
metrics.definition: Monthly spending divided by the real hourly wage.

levers.text: Every line costs hours; the big three cost the most.
Fewer unpaid hours raise the real wage and lower the count.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your hours of work a month of life costs: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Picture completeness
metrics.clientLabel: How much of the picture is in
metrics.definition: The share of the dollars in the picture that are known or verified; a guess counts as not in.

levers.text: Confirm the biggest rough spending lines first.
A statement balance replaces a rough one.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your how much of the picture is in: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Blind spot
metrics.clientLabel: The share of spending your gut did not see
metrics.definition: Of actual spending, the share that the gut guesses did not cover, from the transactions compared with what was said.

levers.text: Tracking the real lines closes it.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your the share of spending your gut did not see: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Guesses left
metrics.clientLabel: Lines still standing in for yours
metrics.definition: Spending areas still filled by a national-average guess instead of her own lines.

levers.text: Type the real line and the guess leaves.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your lines still standing in for yours: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Cushion steps covered
metrics.definition: How many of the three cushion steps the cash pot covers: a lean month, a full month, the full cushion.

levers.text: Cash in the savings account covers the next step.
A lower lean month makes step one easier.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your steps of the cushion covered: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Money stress score
metrics.definition: The latest money stress score the client gave, 1 calm to 10 keeps her up at night.

levers.text: A cushion in the bank is the biggest calm.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your how money feels, 1 to 10: {value}. Down is the direction we want, and every step counts.

metrics.name: Goals on track
metrics.clientLabel: Goals that land by their date
metrics.definition: Of the goals with a date, how many the timeline reaches by that date.

levers.text: A smaller month frees money for the goals.
A smaller goal lands sooner.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your goals that land by their date: {value}. Up is the direction we want, and it has been moving since you started.

metrics.name: Satisfaction with where the money goes
metrics.clientLabel: How satisfied you are with where your money goes
metrics.definition: The latest answer to "how satisfied are you with where your money is going right now", 1 to 10, asked at every session close and money date.

levers.text: Move money from what you rated low to what you rated high; satisfaction can rise while spending rises.
Goals funded on time.
Cushion steps reached.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your satisfaction with where your money goes: {value}. This is the one number that can go up while spending goes up.

metrics.name: Worth-it score per area
metrics.clientLabel: How much each area was worth to you
metrics.definition: Per spending area, "was this worth it" from 1 to 10, with the area's share of spending beside it.
metrics.formula: latest worth-it score per area, with the area's monthly cost and share
metrics.gentleCopy: What each area was worth to you: {value}.

metrics.name: Value per dollar by area
metrics.clientLabel: Where the money buys the most for you
metrics.definition: Each area's worth-it score against its share of spending. High spend with a low score is the easy place to cut; low spend with a high score is where there is room to spend more.
metrics.formula: worth-it score per $1,000 a month; flags: share above 10% with score 4 or lower, share under 10% with score 8 or higher
metrics.gentleCopy: Where the money buys the most for you: {value}.

metrics.name: Safe to spend today
metrics.definition: Cash outside the cushion, minus everything due before the next paycheck, minus the floor, from the cash flow calendar's day-by-day run.
metrics.formula: cash (not the cushion) - committed before next income - floor

levers.text: A bill moved past payday, or a smaller everyday spend before it.
More in checking at the start of the month.

metrics.gentleCopy: Safe to spend today: {value}. Everything due before your next paycheck is already set aside.

metrics.name: Lowest point in the next two months
metrics.definition: The lowest the checking balance gets over the next sixty days, and the day it happens, from the cash flow calendar.
metrics.formula: min over days of the checking balance

levers.text: Move a due date past payday; the bill timing fixer finds the best move.
A bigger starting balance lifts every day.

metrics.gentleCopy: Your tightest day in the next two months lands at {value}. The calendar shows which bill makes it tight.

metrics.name: Car and transport share of gross
metrics.definition: Transportation spending divided by gross pay, read against the 20/3/8 rule (under 8%) and the common 20/4/10 (under 10%).

levers.text: A cheaper car, a shorter loan, or no car in a transit city.

sources.label: Money Guy 20/3/8: car costs under 8% of gross

metrics.gentleCopy: Getting around takes {value} of your pay. The Car calculator shows what each choice would make it.
